question.text: Decomposition of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">X</mi></math> exhibits a rate constant of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>0</mn><mo>.05</mo><mtext> </mtext><mi>μg</mi><mo>/</mo><mi>year</mi></math>. How many years are required for the decomposition of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>5</mn><mtext> </mtext><mi>μg</mi></math> of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">X</mi></math> into <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>2</mn><mo>.5</mo><mtext> </mtext><mi>μg</mi></math>?

solution.text:
According to unit of rate constant, it is a zero order reaction. Then, half life of reaction will be:

t12=C02k=5μg2×0.05μg/year=50 year
